summary: Multi-document priming causes streaming to stall when requesting very large max_tokens
description:
Issue summary: Customer reports repeated stalls and eventual client-side timeouts when making streaming generation requests that prime the model with 8-12 large documents and set max_tokens to 65k. Impact: Customer facing production outage for document summarization pipeline; multiple jobs failing and increased support load. Environment: prod, us-east-1, Dedicated edge routing to serving-runtime clusters.

Observed behavior: Streams start and return first few partial chunks (~1-2s), then stall for 40-90s and eventually client times out with HTTP 504 or streaming websocket disconnect. Server does not emit 5xx in API gateway logs but serving runtime shows long tail processing and repeated KV cache evictions.

Expected behavior: Streaming responses should proceed at consistent per-token latency for the configured max_tokens budget and large prefix, or fail fast with a clear 5xx that indicates resource exhaustion.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Upload 10 documents to prompt_context array (total ~180k tokens priming)
2) Call /v1/chat/stream with model redwood-3b-v2, max_tokens=65000, stream=true, temperature=0.2
3) Observe initial chunks emitted then stream stalls and client disconnects after 60s timeout.

Customer-provided artifacts: request/response HAR, websocket trace, sample prompt files, PMP job IDs.
steps_to_reproduce: Prepare 8-12 long documents totaling ~150k-200k tokens as multi-document primer.
Make a streaming generation request to /v1/chat/stream with max_tokens=65000 and stream enabled.
Watch for initial chunks then prolonged stall and eventual client-side timeout or 504.
Repeat with shorter primer (<10k tokens) to confirm requests succeed normally.

customer_impact: Multiple production jobs for GlobeDocs summarization pipeline are failing; customer reports >50% requests time out or disconnect. Revenue-impacting and blocking go-live for new enterprise integration.
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: KV cache thrashing under heavy prime leading to repeated disk-backed reloads and large GC in worker process.
Observed serving-runtime tail latency with token_loop spikes and backlog growth consistent with blocking operations during finalization of large prefix.
Checked autoscaler: no recent scale-downs during the incident window. Dedicated GPUs at ~78% utilization. No preemption events recorded.
Reproduced internally with a smaller test harness: streaming stalls when primer >120k tokens and max_tokens >50k; CPU on host spikes during stall.
Gateway returned 200 on initial upgrade to stream, so client disconnects due to no data; intermediate keep-alive not being emitted during stall.
impact_timeline: 2026-03-09T18:10:00Z - GlobeDocs began a large batch run of summarizations.
2026-03-09T18:12:34Z - First customer report: streaming hung after initial chunks.
2026-03-09T18:20:00Z - Support triage assigned and ticket opened.

comments: Aisha Patel (Support): Customer reports repeatable stall behavior with exact prompt bundle attached. Asking engineering for triage.
Jordan Lee (SRE): Confirmed elevated tail_latency in serving-runtime logs. Collecting pprof and heap profiles from affected workers.
Marta Rodriguez (Eng): Noted KV cache eviction count unusually high; requesting core dumps and kernel OOM checks.
GlobeDocs support contact (via email): Providing additional priming docs and allowed window for repro. Asks for ETA on mitigation.
Jordan Lee (SRE): Applied temporary proxy keep-alive every 15s to client as a short-term mitigation to avoid client-side timeouts while we dig deeper.
temporary_workarounds: Advise customer to reduce max_tokens to <=20k or split generation into multiple shorter calls.
Enable proxy-side periodic keep-alive to prevent client disconnect during investigation.
Use model variant with lower KV pressure (lora-13b-extended appears to reduce eviction frequency in test).
root_cause_hypothesis: Large multi-document primers cause sustained KV cache thrashing and worker-level blocking (GC or disk IO) during finalization when combined with very large max_tokens, which in turn stalls the streaming pipeline and prevents periodic chunks from being emitted to the client.
resolution_notes: Workaround provided to customer: split prompts and lower max_tokens; applied proxy keep-alive to reduce client disconnects.

Engineering action items: add backpressure controls to detect sustained KV eviction spikes, emit interim keep-alives from streaming pipeline, and add a fast-fail path when primer size + max_tokens exceed safe thresholds for the chosen model variant.
Follow-up: Schedule Q2 change to serving-runtime to avoid blocking kernel during KV reloads and add metrics for primer token counts per request for SLO-driven routing.
next_steps: Eng will instrument primer_size histogram and add alert for >100k primer tokens per request.
Platform will implement optional request-level preflight check that warns or rejects requests that combine very large primers with huge max_tokens.
Customer success to coordinate with GlobeDocs on staged rollout of fixes and acceptance testing.
